claims.body: The Predators get in close, but the Sharks mostly shoot from distance. Nashville is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and San Jose is one of the worst. notes.text: Jonathan Marchessault is day to day (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.

Nicolas Hague has not dressed for the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Daemon Hunt has taken his spot beside Jayden Struble. That pair has had 41% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 83:43 together, up from 29% with Hague.
Shane Wright joined from SEA on Nov 2 and has played beside Filip Forsberg and Nils Höglander.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the third-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 44% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 52:56 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Alexander Wennberg is day to day, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Dmitry Orlov.

stakes: The Predators go in second in the Central with 27 points, the Sharks fifth in the Pacific with 18 points.

story.head: Josi’s favorite opponent
paras: The Predators have won seven straight, and they’re rolling. The Sharks (8-11-2) lost 3-2 in a shootout to Pittsburgh on Wednesday. The Sharks won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in Nashville on Oct 15. The Sharks played last night, and the Predators are rested. Going in, the Predators are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Sharks fifth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd).
The Predators’ record (.675) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.531), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Sharks’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth.
In their seven-game winning streak, the Predators have outscored teams 23-12, including 17-10 at 5-on-5.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Nashville has allowed 2.60 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. On the other side, the Sharks ice the puck a lot (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (31st). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), so the Preds get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. San Jose has scored 2.43 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. Both teams like to play fast, especially the Predators (3rd), so expect an open game.

Roman Josi (2 G / 21 A / 23 P in 20 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with a point in nine straight games against San Jose. Steven Stamkos (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eleven goals. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (8 G / 15 A / 23 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and five goals in seven games against Nashville since 2023-24.

Alex Nedeljkovic (3-3-1 / .895 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for San Jose. Nashville has two options in net: Juuse Saros (7-3-4 / .922 SV% in 14 GS) and Justus Annunen (4-1-0 / .885 SV% in 5 GS). Saros has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
